Can they do anything at all? Kotaku spoke to two T-shirt companies known for their official partnerships with developers including MegaCrit, Team Cherry, Sega, and more, and to a professional apparel designer and freelance artist, about why they kinda can’t do anything about this state of affairs, and more specifically, why they don’t have to do anything at all.

To understand the explosion of shitty video game apparel, you have to know how T-shirts have traditionally been made, and how they’re being made now. Glenn O’Neill is the co-founder of The Yetee, a T-shirt and video game merch company that’s been in business for 15 years and is known for its partnership with the Games Done Quick charity speedrunning event.
https://kotaku.com/app/uploads/2026/08/guildrun4.jpg
“We screen print our T-shirts,” he said. “We’ve been doing so since the start, and it is still the highest quality way to print T-shirts.”

In a nutshell, screen printing involves pressing paint through tiny holes in stencils in successive layers to create a finished, full-color image. It’s a long process and involves a lot of equipment and chemicals, increasing the price of the finished product. It also requires space. While you can screen print at home, making T-shirts at scale means you’re gonna need room.

https://kotaku.com/app/uploads/2023/08/cbcfa88617eefefc2b8dd3e9bd64c663-160x160.jpg
